wikivoyage.text:
Eat:
Portuguese cuisine evolved from hearty peasant food drawn from the land and abundant seafood found in the country's lengthy coast with the cows, pigs and goats raised on the limited grazing land of its interior. From these humble origins, spices and condiments brought back to the country during the exploration and colonisation of South America, Africa, the East Indies and the Far East, contributed to the development of what become regarded as 'typical' Portuguese cuisine which inherently, also helped shape the cuisine in the regions under Portuguese influence, from Brazil and Cape Verde to Thailand and Japan. Today, traditional Portuguese cuisine is served alongside the latest trendy and fusion cuisine styles. Several establishments have been awarded Michelin stars.

Soup is an essential first course of a Portuguese meal. The most popular is the Minho speciality, caldo verde, made from kale, potatoes and spiced smoked sausage.

You will see another Portuguese staple bacalhau (salt cod) everywhere. Locals will tell you that there are as many ways to cook this revered dish as there are days in the year, or even more.

The most common of Portugal's delicious fish (peixe) dishes revolve around sole (linguado) and sardines (sardinha) although salmon (salmão) and trout (truta) are also featured heavily, not mentioning the more traditional mackerel (carapau), whiting (pescada), rock bass (robalo), tuna (atum), frog fish (tamboril) and a variety of turbot (cherne).

In most places you will easily find fresh seafood: lobster (lagosta), crab (caranguejo), lavagante, mussels (mexilhões), cockles (vieiras), oysters (ostras), clam (amêijoas), goose barnacles (perceves).

A peculiarity of Portuguese cuisine is the love of rice and rice-based dishes and desserts, a fondness perhaps grown from the Portuguese travels to the East. Among the most popular rice dishes are "Arroz à Bulhão Pato", essentially a juicy rice and clam dish. Another famous rice dish, "Arroz de Cabidela" consisting of a saucy dish made with rice, chicken and its blood. Besides those already mentioned, there are many varieties of rice-based specialities, such as frog fish rice, octopus rice, duck rice and seafood rice.

Depending on how touristy the area you are in, you'll see grills, thick with the smoke of charring meat, in front of many restaurants during your stay. Other than traditional sardines, Portuguese grilled chicken -- marinated in chilli, garlic and olive oil -- is world famous, althou…

response.text:
See:
Lisbon is a city on the water—the River Tagus (Rio Tejo)—built on seven hills that are traversed by trams. This has led to comparisons with San Francisco. To provide access from the southern suburbs, Lisbon has two spectacular bridges. The 25th of April Bridge (Ponte 25 de Abril) combines the design of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge with the color of the Golden Gate Bridge, and it's often mistaken for the latter. The Vasco da Gama Bridge (Ponte Vasco da Gama), Europe's longest, was built in the 1990s for Expo '98. One of Lisbon's great landmarks, Cristo Rei, a 28 m statue of Christ the King on an 82 m pedestal, isn't even in Lisbon itself, but across the river in Almada, big enough to be easily seen from the capital.

Alfama:
Built on the hills east of the Baixa, Alfama survived the Great 1755 Earthquake largely intact. Climbing the narrow ancient lanes provides an excellent workout. You can spare your legs by taking the little historic yellow trams that serve the neighborhood. Major sights include Lisbon Cathedral and St. George's Castle.

Bairro Alto:
The Bairro Alto, or "Upper District" (dare we say "High Neighbourhood"), has become Lisbon's youthful, trendy quarter. The district includes the Chiado neighbourhood, known for its numerous historic landmarks and theatres. Among the district's many sights are the São Bento Palace (where the Portuguese parliament meets), the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (a museum of antique art), and the Lisbon Botanical Gardens.

response.text:
Eat:
Portuguese dining rituals tend to follow the Mediterranean siesta body clock. Most restaurants are very small, family-run and generally inexpensive. Some of them have a sheet on the door with the pratos do dia (dishes of the day) written on it – these dishes are usually cheaper and fresher than the rest of menu there, and unless you're looking for something specific, they're the right choice. During the dinner the waiter will probably bring you some unrequested starter dishes (called couvert); as those are not free, don't feel obliged to touch them and they will not be charged on your bill (but check it!).

Traditional Portuguese restaurants are in Bairro Alto, scattered abundantly through its quirky narrow streets, and for Portuguese traditional cuisine at its finest, head to the area of Chiado. Tour groups primarily feel at home in Alfama. Tourist traps with laminated menus and meal deals are mostly concentrated in the Baixa area; one exception to this is the Rua das Portas de Santo Antão, a 'seafood strip' northeast from and parallel to Praça dos Restauradores. If you feel like eating with the local people, try the Castelo neighborhood, the smaller family run places serve a fixed daily menu and are not expensive, getting up there by foot will open an appetite, or else go in the elétrico. For a familiar taste at one of the many chain eateries, head to Doca de Santo Amaro (train/tram 15 station Alcantara-Mar) and Parque das Nações (metro Oriental). All the culinary and …

results.name: Leitaria Camponeza
results.summary: On the location of a historical café (the leitaria), this place focuses on only a short number of dishes (meats, fish and seafood) but makes up for this in quality and portion size. For an atmospheric presentation ask for one of their espetadas. The wines complement the dishes and you can end the meal with a dessert. For someone looking for great value for their buck (no compromises on quality), it's a good place to start or end an evening. Price: €15-30

results.name: Mercado da Praça da Figueira
results.summary: From the pavement looks like a small convenience shop, on walking in you realize the deception when confronted by the large cavernous meandering interior space, replete with everything expected from a well stocked supermarket. Although there isn't a restaurant as such, the ready to eat items on offer are tasty, fresh, inexpensive and varied. The sandwiches and hamburgers are superb.

results.name: Mercado Oriental
results.summary: A food court serving Asian street food and the only place in Lisbon where you can try Macanese cuisine (at a stall called "Taberna Macau"). Price: Small dishes €3

results.name: Néctar WineBar
results.summary: A place dedicated to the promotion of Portugal's wine and gastronomic culture, and featuring a daily lunch menu of Portuguese and Mediterranean cuisine. The wine list comprises – in its vast majority – a selection of Portuguese wines which best represent the country. Wine can be bought by the glass, and it is served at the appropriate temperatures and in suitable glasses. Dishes – served in portions for 2 – easily replace a main course meal. Homemade-style desserts, for which sweet wines can be suggested. A modern and cosy atmosphere. Price: €25-35

results.name: Ajuda Botanical Gardens
results.summary: The botanical garden of Ajuda is one of the oldest gardens in Europe and is considered the first in Portugal. After the earthquake that occurred in 1755, the homeless Portuguese royal family decided to build a new royal residence at Ajuda but also gardens around it. This 10-acre garden was laid out in from 1858-1873.

results.name: Centro Cultural de Belém
results.summary: CCB is a 140000 m² complex of artistic and cultural venues. It has spaces for meetings and conferences, performing arts (film, opera, ballet, theatre, and music), and art exhibits (art, architecture, design, and photography).

results.name: Monument to the Discoveries
results.summary: Climbing the monument gives you a spectacular view of Belém.

results.name: Mosteiro dos Jerónimos
results.summary: A , the monastery was built in the 16th century and is an outstanding example of the Portuguese late Gothic Manueline style. Price: €18 (adults), €9 (seniors/students/youth card), free (children under 12); free admission to the church and on first Sun of the month. Note that tickets are sold from the neighbouring archeological museum, not at the monastery entrance
results.hours: Oct-May: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:30; May-Sep: Tue-Sun 10:00-18:30; last entry 30 min before closing; closed 1 Jan, Easter, 1 May, 13 Jun, and 25 Dec

results.name: Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology
results.summary: This museum of contemporary art is housed in a riverside building of contemporary design. Price: Adults , kids 12+/students/seniors 65+ , kids under 12 free,15 Jul–31 Aug: 20% discount off all tickets (admission includes Tejo Power Station)
results.hours: Wed–Mon 11:00–19:00 (Jun–Sep: Fri Sat until 22:00), closed Tue

results.name: Museu Colecção Berardo
results.summary: The permanent collection of the museum consists of the Berardo Collection, which is made up of modern and contemporary art, with major art movements like abstract expressionism, Abstraction-Création, action painting, body Art, constructivism, cubism, De Stijl, digital art, experimental art, geometric abstraction, kinetic art, minimal art, neo-expressionism, neo-plasticism, neo-Realism, op art, photography, photorealism, pop art, realism, suprematism, surrealism. Includes artists like Piet Mondrian, Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein, Pablo Picasso and Jackson Pollock, and Francis Bacon.

results.name: Museu da Marinha
results.summary: One of the most important in Europe, evoking Portugal's domination of the seas. Its colossal 17,000 items are installed in the west wing of Jerónimos Monastery, and include model ships from the Age of Discovery onward. The oldest exhibit is a wooden figure representing the Archangel Raphael that accompanied Vasco da Gama on his voyage to India. Price: Adults , seniors 65+ & youths 4–12 , kids 0–3 free, family (2 adults & 2 youths)

results.name: Museu Nacional dos Coches
results.summary: Housed in the former riding school of the palace, don't miss the world's largest collection of horse-drawn coaches and other royal vehicles. One of Lisbon's many unusual museums. In the "Museum street", Belem.

results.name: Planetário Calouste Gulbenkian
results.summary: The planetarium has 32 star projectors, capable of presenting more than 9,000 stars. It holds a chunk of moon rock given by U.S. President Richard Nixon. Price: Adults , seniors 65+ & kids 4-12 , kids 0-3 free, family (2 adults & 2 youths)
results.hours: Temporarily closed for renovations; planned reopening Oct 2021

results.name: Ponte 25 de Abril
results.summary: This sister bridge of the San Francisco – Oakland Bay Bridge was designed by the same architect in 1966 to connect Lisbon with the Setubal peninsula across the Tagus (Tejo) River. Formerly known as the Salazar Bridge, it was renamed after the Carnation Revolution which, on 25 April 1974, ended the dictatorship.

results.name: Statue to Afonso de Albuquerque
results.summary: In front of the former Royal Palace of Belém, now the Presidential Palace, there is a massive statue looking out to sea, representing Afonso de Albuquerque, second ruler of Portuguese India in the early 16th century.

results.name: Tejo Power Station
results.summary: This disused power station is now a museum dedicated to the science, industry, and history of electricity production in Portugal. Price: Admission included in the price of the Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology

results.name: Torre de Belém
results.summary: A , the iconic fortified tower was built in the early 16th century in the late Gothic Manueline style as a fortress. It was said to be the last thing Portuguese explorers saw when departing, and the first thing they saw upon return. It was later used as a prison for political prisoners, and is today one of the most recognized symbols of Lisbon and Portugal. Price: €6 (adults), €3 (seniors/students/youth card), free (children under 12); free admission on first Sun of the month. Combined ticket with Mosteiro dos Jerónimos €12, combined ticket with Mosteiro dos Jerónimos and Museu Nacional de Arq

results.name: Museu da Carris
results.summary: Transport museum with various old trams and buses on display. Price: €4.50, €2.50 for over 65s, under 6 free

results.name: Restaurante Sinal Vermelho

results.name: Café Buenos Aires

results.name: Belcanto

results.name: Loco Restaurante

results.name: 100 Maneiras

results.title: São Jorge Castle
results.extract: São Jorge Castle (Portuguese: Castelo de São Jorge; Portuguese pronunciation: [kɐʃˈtɛlu dɨ sɐ̃w̃ ˈʒɔɾʒɨ]), sometimes known in English as Saint George's Castle, is a historic castle in the Portuguese capital of Lisbon, located in the freguesia of Santa Maria Maior. Human occupation of the castle hill dates to at least the 8th century BC while the oldest fortifications on the site date from the 2nd century BC. The hill on which Saint George's Castle stands has played an important part in the history of Lisbon, having served as the location of fortifications occupied successively by Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors, before its conquest by the Portuguese in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon. Since the 12th century, the castle has variously served as a royal palace, a military barracks, home of the Torre do Tombo National Archive, and now as a national monument and museum.

results.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
results.summary: Good viewpoint in Alfama uphill from the cathedral along tram route. Lovely view over rooftops and river.

results.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
results.summary: The highest viewpoint in Lisbon, at the top of the Graça hill, spread out in front of the small Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monte (founded in 1147, remodelled in the 20th century). To the south you look down over the Castelo de São Jorge, the Mouraria and the Baixa to the Tagus estuary; to the west, from Bairro Alto out to the Monsanto forest; to the north, down the Avenida Almirante Reis valley. It sits a little further out than the viewpoints at Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol, so it is usually quieter, and it is a fine place to watch the sunset.

results.name: Castelo de São Jorge
results.summary: Humans settled on this hill as early as the 8th century BCE, and the first fortifications date from the 1st century BCE. Before the Portuguese conquest in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon, the site was successively occupied by the Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors. Sights within the castle include the permanent exhibition of archaeological artefacts with an emphasis on the 11th- and 12th-century Moors, ruins of the former Royal Palace of Alcáçova, a garden with native forest species, and a camera obscura showing the city's sights. The castle offers great view over the city and the river. I

results.name: Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
results.summary: Started in 1582, this Mannerist monastery wasn't completed until 1629, following the reconstruction of a 1147 church under royal decree. The church houses the Pantheon of the House of Braganza, where many monarchs, consorts, and their offspring are entombed.

results.name: Lisbon Cathedral
results.summary: Built in 1147, the cathedral has survived various earthquakes and has undergone restoration, renovation, and modification over the years. Its elements include Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. It has been a national monument since 1910. Price: , children 7–12 , children 6 & under free

results.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
results.summary: One of the most important national museums, dedicated to Portuguese azulejo tiles since the late 1400s. It's in the former Madre de Deus Convent, founded in 1509 by Queen Leonor. Price: , seniors 65+/students/youth card , disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu Militar de Lisboa
results.summary: Housed in a 16th-century foundry, this museum holds its testaments to Portuguese military history, and contains many artifacts, including a sword used by Vasco da Gama.

results.name: Museu de Sociedade de Geografia
results.summary: Exhibits of ethnography from Portugal's former colonies. Price: , seniors 65+ , students & youths , families of 4 or more  each, disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu do Teatro Romano
results.summary: Along the way from downtown to Saint George's Castle.

results.name: Panteão Nacional
results.summary: This is one of the most striking buildings in Lisbon. Its tall dome and white facade makes it a real landmark in Alfama/Eastern Lisbon. Excellent views from the rooftop terrace. Construction began in 1681, then halted until the dome was added in 1966 and then converted to the National Pantheon. Amália Rodrigues, queen of fado, is buried here, and fresh roses can be seen on the tomb. The church also has wide viewing platform on the rooftop all around its dome. Excellent panorama of the river and surroundings. No elevator.

response.answer: Bacalhau à brás is a traditional Portuguese dish made with shredded salt cod, onions, and thinly fried potato matchsticks, all bound with eggs. The dish is usually garnished with black olives and fresh cilantro or parsley. The main ingredients include salt cod, potatoes, eggs, and onion. The origin of the recipe is uncertain, but it is said to have originated in the late 19th century in Bairro Alto, Lisbon. The name "à brás" is believed to come from a 19th-century Lisbon tavern or restaurant called Braz. We need to produce comparison output based on given Airbnb and hotel options, using the brief (mid budget 2500 total). Need to group by area (neighbourhood). Areas not specified directly; we have lat/lon and distances from centre. We can infer areas: central Lisbon (Baixa), Alfheim? Let's deduce based on proximity: 

Airbnb list:
- Double Bedroom with TV, Pool... 10.1 km from centre -> likely outside central, maybe outskirts (maybe suburb). No area label, but we can categorize as "Outskirts".
- Marta's House 1.1 km from centre -> central, likely Baixa/Chiado.
- GuestReady duplex in Alfama 2.3 km from centre, but location is Alfama.
- Villa Tejo II 7.3 km from centre -> outskirts.
- Príncipe Real ... 1.2 km from centre -> Príncipe Real area.
- Charming room ... 1.2 km from centre -> central (maybe Baixa).
- Amazing & Lovely - Heart of Alfama 2.4 km from centre -> Alfama.
- The Restauradores Collection — Regal 1.3 km from centre -> central (Restauradores street near Baixa).

Hotel list:
- Green View Home lat 38.738565 -9.1523872, near maybe Avenidas, outskirts?
- Alfama - Lisbon Lounge Suites lat 38.713632 -9.128602 -> Alfama.
- My Charm Lisbon Suites lat 38.7309571 -9.1342926 -> central.
- Famous Crows Guest House lat 38.697439 -9.2029665 -> outskirts (Alcântara?).
- Residencial Valentina lat 38.7113435 -9.153175 -> central.
- Rossio Plaza Hotel lat 38.712395 -9.139096 -> Baixa/Rossio.
- HF Fénix Urban lat 38.728753 -9.149 -> central.

We need at most 6 areas, most central / best-covered first. Let's choose: Alfama, Baixa/Restauradores (central), Príncipe Real, Outskirts (general), maybe "Lisbon Centre" as catch-all.

But we need grouping by area and include best Airbnb and best hotel per area, and min_price_per_night_eur.

Let's define areas based on proximity string in details if present, else lat. Use these areas:

1. Alfama (includes Airbnb GuestReady duplex, Amazing & Lovely, and hotel Alfama - Lisbon Lounge Suites)
2. Baixa/Restauradores (includes Marta's House, Charming room, Restauradores collection, hotel Rossio Plaza Hotel, Residencial Valentina, My Charm Lisbon Suites)
3. Príncipe Real (Airbnb Príncipe Real, maybe hotels not there)
4. Outskirts/Suburban (Airbnb Double Bedroom with pool, Villa Tejo II, hotel Green View Home, Famous Crows Guest House, HF Fénix Urban perhaps central but still)
5. Could also include "Central Lisbon" as generic.

But we need at most 6 areas, okay.

Now determine best Airbnb per area based on rating/price tradeoff. "Best" as good rating for low price. We'll compute rating (out of 5) and price per night.

Airbnbs:
- Alfama:
   - GuestReady duplex: rating null, price/night 109.95.
   - Amazing & Lovely: rating 4.67, price/night 144.0.
Pick GuestReady rating null can't compare; pick one with highest rating among those with reasonable price? The clear best rating is 4.67 (Amazing & Lovely) but higher price. Maybe choose GuestReady with unknown rating but cheaper. However the rule "best = good rating for a low price". I'd choose Amazing & Lovely because rating decent. But price is higher. Could also choose GuestReady as unknown rating (null) can't evaluate. I'd select Amazing & Lovely.

- Baixa/Restauradores:
   Airbnb options: Marta's House rating 4.86 price 89.0/night, Charming room rating 4.86 price 131.5/night, Restauradores collection rating 4.9 price 198.5/night.
Best rating 4.9 but high price. Best value likely Marta's House (high rating 4.86, lower price). So choose Marta's House.

- Príncipe Real:
   Only Príncipe Real Airbnb rating 4.78 price 130.93/night.

- Outskirts:
   Double Bedroom with pool rating 4.98 price 58/night, Villa Tejo II rating 5.0 price 127.75/night.
Best rating 5.0 but price higher. Best value maybe Double Bedroom with pool (rating 4.98 close, cheapest). So choose that.

- Additional area maybe "Central Lisbon" but already covered.

Now hotels per area:

- Alfama: Alfama - Lisbon Lounge Suites rating 4.3 price 69.75/night. Also maybe HF Fénix Urban not Alfama but central. So best in Alfama = Alfama Lounge Suites.

- Baixa/Restauradores: Rossio Plaza Hotel rating (converted) 9.2/10 => 4.6/5, price per night 109.44. Residencial Valentina rating 4.4 price 80.0. My Charm Lisbon Suites rating 4.2 price 70.75. Which is best value? Likely My Charm (price low, rating decent). Best rating among hotels: Rossio (4.6) but price high. We'll pick My Charm Lisbon Suites as best value and also lowest price per night.

- Príncipe Real: No hotel listed; null.

- Outskirts: Green View Home rating 4.1 price 44.0, Famous Crows Guest House rating 4.3 price 71.0, HF Fénix Urban rating 8.6/10 -> 4.3, price 110.83. Best rating vs price: maybe Green View Home low price but rating 4.1, Famous Crows rating 4.3 higher price. Choose Green View Home as cheapest and decent rating.

Now overall cheapest stay across all: find lowest total_price_eur.

Airbnbs totals: double bedroom 232, Marta 356, GuestReady 439.8, Villa 511, Príncipe Real 523.7, Charming 526, Amazing 576, Restauradores 794.

Hotels totals: Green View 176, Alfama Lounge 279, My Charm 283, Famous Crows 284, Residencial Valentina 320, Rossio Plaza 437.77, HF Fénix Urban 443.34.

Cheapest total price is Green View Home (176). So cheapest stay is that hotel.

Best value overall: need balance of price, rating, location. Likely Marta's House (Airbnb) price 356, rating 4.86, central location (1.1 km). Hotels like My Charm 283 rating 4.2, location central but rating lower. So best value likely Marta's House.

Top rated (highest rating 0-5 scale): Among stays, Villa Tejo II rating 5.0 (Airbnb). Also Double Bedroom rating 4.98, close. So top rating is Villa Tejo II (5.0). Note hotel ratings converted: Rossio 4.6, HF Fénix 4.3. So top_rated = Villa Tejo II.

Now assemble "by_area" list up to 6 areas.

We'll include:

{

 airbnb: Amazing & Lovely - Heart of Alfama,
 hotel: Alfama - Lisbon Lounge Suites,
 min_price_per_night_eur: (minimum among both?). Need the lowest price_per_night_eur among stays in area. In Alfama: Airbnb Amazing 144, hotel 69.75. So min = 69.75.
}

{

 min_price_per_night_eur: min(89.0, 70.75) = 70.75 (or 70.75)
}

results.name: Lisbon City Hall
results.summary: Lisbon City Hall (Paços do Concelho de Lisboa) is the seat of the municipal government, located on Praça do Município. Built in the neoclassical style after the 1755 earthquake, it features a grand façade with sculptures and a notable central staircase designed by José Luís Monteiro. The building was reconstructed between 1865 and 1880 following a fire that destroyed the original hall.

results.name: Monumento a Camões
results.summary: The Camões Monument stands in Luís de Camões Square in Chiado, honoring Portugal’s national poet Luis de Camões. Unveiled in 1867, the bronze statue is set on a lioz limestone pillar surrounded by eight smaller figures of notable figures from the Age of Discoveries. It was sculpted by Victor Bastos and inaugurated in the presence of King Luís I and Ferdinand II.

results.name: Muralha Fernandina
results.summary: The Cerca Fernandina (Fernandina Walls) are medieval fortifications built in 1373 by King Fernando I, extending the earlier Roman walls of Lisbon. These walls marked the city's expansion during the 14th century and are an important historical remnant of Lisbon’s defensive architecture.

results.name: National Museum of Archaeology
results.summary: The National Museum of Archaeology, housed in the western wing of the Jerónimos Monastery, was founded in 1893 by José Leite de Vasconcelos and opened in 1906. It holds the largest archaeological collection in Portugal, showcasing artifacts from the Iberian Peninsula and the Mediterranean, and its Neo‑Manueline building reflects historicist architecture of the early 20th century.

results.name: Navy Museum
results.summary: The Navy Museum (Museu de Marinha) occupies part of the neo‑Manueline western wing of the Jerónimos Monastery and a modern annex, presenting Portugal’s maritime heritage. Established in 1963, its collections include ship models, navigation instruments, paintings and the historic Fairey III “Santa Cruz” aircraft, illustrating centuries of Portuguese exploration.

args.markdown_text:
# Lisbon trip guide: 2027-05-10 – 2027-05-14

Two adults travelling from Helsinki to Lisbon for five days (four nights).  Budget tier: **mid** with a total budget of **€2 500**.  Interests are history and street food.  The weather forecast is based on typical conditions for these dates (light rain to overcast, 12‑20 °C).

## Getting there and back

**Chosen flights**

| | Mode | Operator | Depart → Arrive | Duration | Stops | Price (all travellers) | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Outbound (chosen)** | flight | SAS | 2027-05-10 11:15 → 2027-05-10 16:10 | 415 min | 1 | €297 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/jwhvkp) |
| **Return (chosen)** | flight | Finnair | 2027-05-14 16:35 → 2027-05-14 23:10 | 275 min | 0 | €387 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

**Outbound alternatives**

| | Mode | Operator | Depart → Arrive | Duration | Stops | Price (all travellers) | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cheapest** | flight | Ryanair, easyJet | 2027-05-10 23:15 → 2027-05-11 09:55 | 760 min | 1 | €293 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/fg5t4x3) |
| **Fastest** | flight | Finnair | 2027-05-10 13:00 → 2027-05-10 15:50 | 290 min | 0 | €411 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/p663wh) |

> **Note:** The cheapest outbound option requires an airport change in Copenhagen (STN → LTN) and self‑transfer between terminals.

**Return alternatives**

| | Mode | Operator | Depart → Arrive | Duration | Stops | Price (all travellers) | Link |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cheapest** | flight | Ryanair, SAS | 2027-05-14 06:50 → 2027-05-14 20:25 | 695 min | 2 | €283 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/3xgwh26) |
| **Fastest** (chosen) | flight | Finnair | 2027-05-14 16:35 → 2027-05-14 23:10 | 275 min | 0 | €387 (live) | [details](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

> **Note:** The cheapest return option involves two airport changes (Lisbon → AGP → ARN → HEL) and requires self‑transfer.

## Where to stay

**Chosen accommodation:** [Marta's House](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/9152658?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) (Airbnb) – 1 km from the historic centre, 4 nights at **€89 / night**, total **€356 (live)**, rating **4.86/5**.  Best overall value for a mid‑budget stay.

### Options by area

| Area | Airbnb | Hotel | From €/night |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alfama | [Amazing & Lovely - Heart of Alfama](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/13024533?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) | [Alfama - Lisbon Lounge Suites (Alojamento Local)](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Alfama+-+Lisbon+Lounge+Suites+%28Alojamento+Local%29%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) | €69.75 |
| Baixa/Restauradores | [Marta's House](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/9152658?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) | [My Charm Lisbon Suites](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=My+Charm+Lisbon+Suites%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) | €70.75 |
| Príncipe Real | [Príncipe Real • Air conditioning](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/863721243841940780?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) | – | €130.93 |
| Outskirts | [Double Bedroom with TV, Pool, and Private Bathroom](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/1457105680391230136?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) | [Green View Home](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Green+View+Home%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) | €44.00 |

**Recommendation:** Marta's House offers the highest rating and central location for the price.  Hotel prices shown are from liteAPI and may exclude city tax.

## Day by day

### Day 1 – Mon 2027‑05‑10: Alfama
*Weather:* light rain, 13‑17 °C – **rainy**. *Walk:* 0.9 km.
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with SAS, see *Getting there and back*.
- **17:45 Lisbon Cathedral** – Lisbon’s oldest church, founded in 1147 after the reconquest; blends Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque styles. Open 10:00‑18:30. Ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.patriarcado-lisboa.pt/site/index.php?id=10686)
- **18:45 São Jorge Castle** – Historic hilltop fortress with origins back to the 8th century BC; served as royal palace and military barracks. Open 09:00‑21:00. Ticket price: see the website. [source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Jorge_Castle)
- **20:30 Néctar WineBar** – Mid‑budget wine bar offering Portuguese dishes; good for trying local wines with petiscos. Budget tier: mid. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027‑05‑11: Belém
*Weather:* drizzle, 13‑18 °C – **rainy**. *Walk:* 1.1 km.
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – UNESCO UNESCO monastery, masterpiece of Manueline architecture built to celebrate Vasco da Gama’s voyage. Open 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). Ticket €18. [source](http://www.patrimoniocultural.gov.pt/en/museus-e-monumentos/dgpc/m/mosteiro-dos-jeronimos/)
- **12:30 Lunch near Belém** – Try the iconic **pastel de nata** from a nearby bakery. 
- **13:30 Monument to the Discoveries** – 1960 monument shaped like a caravel prow, commemorating the Age of Discovery; climb for river views. Ticket €4. [source](http://www.padraodosdescobrimentos.pt/)
- **15:00 National Museum of Archaeology** – Holds Portugal’s largest archaeological collection; Neo‑Manueline building. Open 10:00‑18:00. Ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/2491785179)
- **16:30 Navy Museum** – Maritime heritage museum in the western wing of Jerónimos, showcasing ship models and navigation instruments. Open 10:00‑18:00 (May‑Sep). Ticket price: see the website. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/6216727635)
- **19:30 Dinner near Belém** – Sample local seafood at a nearby market (e.g., grilled sardines). 

### Day 3 – Wed 2027‑05‑12: Restauradores
*Weather:* rain, 13‑18 °C – **rainy**. *Walk:* 1.3 km.
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – Sports history museum with trophies, memorabilia and interactive displays. Open 10:00‑17:00. Free entry. [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966)
- **11:45 Monumento aos Restauradores** – Monument commemorating the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. [source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630)
- **12:30 Mercado Oriental** – Asian street‑food market; try the **Macanese** stall for a fusion of Portuguese and Asian flavors. Budget tier: low. Open 12:00‑22:30. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **14:30 Museu Nacional do Azulejo** – Tile museum housed in the former Madre de Deus Convent, tracing azulejo art from the 15th century to today. Open 10:00‑13:00 & 14:00‑18:00 (Tue‑Sun). Ticket price: see the website. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Alfama)

# Lisbon trip guide: 2027-05-10 – 2027-05-14

Two adults travelling from Helsinki on a relaxed, mid‑budget trip (total budget **€2500**). Interests are history and street food. Weather notes are based on typical conditions for these dates, not a forecast.

## Getting there and back

| Return | Flight | Finnair | 2027‑05‑14 16:35 → 2027‑05‑14 23:10 | 275 min (4 h 35 m) | 0 | €387 (live) | [Details](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

| Fastest | Flight | Finnair | 2027‑05‑14 16:35 → 2027‑05‑14 23:10 | 275 min (4 h 35 m) | 0 | €387 (live) | [Details](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |
**Note**: Cheapest return involves two airline changes and three stops.

## Where to stay

## Day by day
### Day 1 – Mon 2027‑05‑10: Baixa / Chiado
*Weather*: light rain · walking 0.3 km
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with SAS; see Getting there and back.
- **17:30 Lisbon Cathedral** – Lisbon’s oldest church, founded in 1147 after the reconquest; blends Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque elements. Open Mon–Sat 10:00‑18:30. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.patriarcado-lisboa.pt/site/index.php?id=10686)
- **20:00 Néctar WineBar** – Mid‑range wine bar, try the house‑made dessert. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027‑05‑11: Belém
*Weather*: drizzle · walking 12.9 km
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – UNESCO Manueline monastery built in the 16th century to celebrate Vasco da Gama’s voyage; includes the Church of Santa Maria de Belém. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). *ticket €18* [Source](http://www.patrimoniocultural.gov.pt/en/museus-e-monumentos/dgpc/m/mosteiro-dos-jeronimos/)
- **12:30 Mercado Oriental** – Street‑food market, try the Macanese stall (small dishes €3). (low budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **13:30 National Museum of Archaeology** – Largest archaeological collection in Portugal, housed in the western wing of the Jerónimos monastery; opened 1906. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.mnarqueologia-ipmuseus.pt/)
- **15:15 Navy Museum** – Maritime heritage exhibits; established 1963, includes ship models and navigation instruments. Open May‑Sep 10:00‑18:00, Oct‑Apr 10:00‑17:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://ccm.marinha.pt/pt/museu)
- **18:30 Dinner near Belém** – Snack from a nearby kiosk.

### Day 3 – Wed 2027‑05‑12: Chiado / Alfama
*Weather*: rain · walking 12.5 km
- **10:00 Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado** – Modern Portuguese and international art, covering painting, sculpture, photography and design. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/96321716)
- **12:00 Museu Arqueológico do Carmo** – Housed in a former convent ruined by the 1755 earthquake; displays archaeological finds from prehistoric to Roman times. Open Oct‑May Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00; Jun‑Sep 10:00‑19:00. *ticket €7* [Source](https://www.museuarqueologicodocarmo.pt/)
- **13:30 Cervejaria da Trindade** – Try the codfish plate; good beer selection. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **14:30 Monumento a Camões** – Bronze statue honoring poet Luís de Camões, unveiled 1867; located in Praça Luís de Camões. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam%C3%B5es_Monument)
- **15:30 Monument to the Discoveries** – Iconic 1960 monument shaped like a caravel prow; climb for river views. *ticket €4* [Source](http://www.padraodosdescobrimentos.pt/)
- **16:30 Muralha Fernandina** – Medieval wall fragment built in 1373 by King Fernando I, part of Lisbon’s 14th‑century defenses. [Source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/N4845258130)
- **19:00 Belcanto** – Two‑Michelin‑star dinner; order the tasting menu. (high budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 4 – Thu 2027‑05‑13: Parque Eduardo VII
*Weather*: drizzle · walking 1.1 km
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – Interactive sport‑history exhibits. Free entry. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑17:00. [Source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966)
- **12:30 Faca & Garfo** – Grilled Portuguese specialties; good value. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **14:00 Monument aos Restauradores** – Commemorates the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. [Source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630)
- **19:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – Traditional Portuguese dishes; three‑course dinner. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 5 – Fri 2027‑05‑14: Avenidas de Lisboa
*Weather*: overcast · walking 1.9 km
- **10:00 Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** – World‑class collections spanning antiquities, European, Islamic and modern art. Open Sun‑Mon, We‑Fr 10:00‑18:00; Sat 10:00‑21:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calouste_Gulbenkian_Museum)
- **12:30 Os Tibetanos** – Vegetarian/vegan friendly; try the tofu stir‑fry. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **16:35 Depart from Lisbon** – Flight with Finnair; see Getting there and back.

- **Caldo verde** – Portuguese soup [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q770977)

- **Cocido** – Spanish or Portuguese dish [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q868158)

**Recommendation**: Green View Home gives the lowest total price (**€176**) while still scoring 4.1/5. If you prefer a private Airbnb with higher rating, the Lisbon double‑bedroom at €232 total is also within the mid‑budget tier. Note: liteAPI hotel rates may be 15‑30 % lower than public rates and exclude city tax.

## Day by day
*Days in this plan start around 09:30 and end by 22:00, at a relaxed pace. For another rhythm, tell the concierge, e.g. "we wake up early, start at 07:00", "we stay out late" or "a more relaxed pace, please".*

### Day 1 – Mon 2027‑05‑10: Baixa / Chiado
*Weather*: light rain · walking 0.3 km
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with SAS; see Getting there and back.
- **17:30 Lisbon Cathedral** – Lisbon’s oldest church, founded in 1147 after the reconquest; blends Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque elements. Open Mon–Sat 10:00‑18:30. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.patriarcado-lisboa.pt/site/index.php?id=10686)
- **20:00 Néctar WineBar** – Mid‑range wine bar, try the house‑made dessert. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027‑05‑11: Belém
*Weather*: drizzle · walking 12.9 km
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – UNESCO Manueline monastery built in the 16th century to celebrate Vasco da Gama’s voyage; includes the Church of Santa Maria de Belém. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). *ticket €18* [Source](http://www.patrimoniocultural.gov.pt/en/museus-e-monumentos/dgpc/m/mosteiro-dos-jeronimos/)
- **12:30 Mercado Oriental** – Street‑food market, try the Macanese stall (small dishes €3). (low budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **13:30 National Museum of Archaeology** – Largest archaeological collection in Portugal, housed in the western wing of the Jerónimos monastery; opened 1906. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.mnarqueologia-ipmuseus.pt/)
- **15:15 Navy Museum** – Maritime heritage exhibits; established 1963, includes ship models and navigation instruments. Open May‑Sep 10:00‑18:00, Oct‑Apr 10:00‑17:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://ccm.marinha.pt/pt/museu)
- **18:30 Dinner near Belém** – Snack from a nearby kiosk.

### Day 3 – Wed 2027‑05‑12: Chiado / Alfama
*Weather*: rain · walking 12.5 km
- **10:00 Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado** – Modern Portuguese and international art, covering painting, sculpture, photography and design. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/96321716)
- **12:00 Museu Arqueológico do Carmo** – Housed in a former convent ruined by the 1755 earthquake; displays archaeological finds from prehistoric to Roman times. Open Oct‑May Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00; Jun‑Sep 10:00‑19:00. *ticket €7* [Source](https://www.museuarqueologicodocarmo.pt/)
- **13:30 Cervejaria da Trindade** – Try the codfish plate; good beer selection. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **14:30 Monumento a Camões** – Bronze statue honoring poet Luís de Camões, unveiled 1867; located in Praça Luís de Camões. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam%C3%B5es_Monument)
- **15:30 Monument to the Discoveries** – Iconic 1960 monument shaped like a caravel prow; climb for river views. *ticket €4* [Source](http://www.padraodosdescobrimentos.pt/)
- **16:30 Muralha Fernandina** – Medieval wall fragment built in 1373 by King Fernando I, part of Lisbon’s 14th‑century defenses. [Source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/N4845258130)
- **19:00 Belcanto** – Two‑Michelin‑star dinner; order the tasting menu. (high budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 4 – Thu 2027‑05‑13: Parque Eduardo VII
*Weather*: drizzle · walking 1.1 km
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – Interactive sport‑history exhibits. Free entry. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑17:00. [Source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966)
- **12:30 Faca & Garfo** – Grilled Portuguese specialties; good value. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **14:00 Monument aos Restauradores** – Commemorates the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. [Source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630)
- **19:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – Traditional Portuguese dishes; three‑course dinner. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 5 – Fri 2027‑05‑14: Avenidas de Lisboa
*Weather*: overcast · walking 1.9 km
- **10:00 Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** – World‑class collections spanning antiquities, European, Islamic and modern art. Open Sun‑Mon, We‑Fr 10:00‑18:00; Sat 10:00‑21:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calouste_Gulbenkian_Museum)
- **12:30 Os Tibetanos** – Vegetarian/vegan friendly; try the tofu stir‑fry. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **16:35 Depart from Lisbon** – Flight with Finnair; see Getting there and back.

## Food to try
- **Caldo verde** – Portuguese soup [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q770977)
- **Pastel de nata** – Portuguese egg tart pastry dusted with cinnamon [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421401)
- **Feijoada** – Bean and meat stew popular in Portuguese‑speaking areas [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q878189)
- **Francesinha** – Portuguese sandwich [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q732)
- **Fios de ovos** – Portuguese egg dessert [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q3275692)
- **Cocido** – Spanish or Portuguese dish [Source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q868158)

## Cost estimate
| Category | Total (€) | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | 684.0 | 42.8 % |
| Stay | 176.0 | 11.0 % |
| Food | 600.0 | 37.5 % |
| Activities | 58.0 | 3.6 % |
| Local transport | 80.0 | 5.0 % |
| **Total** | **1598.0** | **63.9 %** |

**Per person**: €799 total; €159.8 per day.

**Assumptions**:
- Food: typical mid‑budget cost of €50 per person per day.
- Local transport: typical €8 per person per day.
- Extra €100 for planned restaurants above the mid budget (typical meal: low €15, mid €30, high €80 per person).
- 8 sights with unknown ticket price counted as €0.

**Budget comparison**: Planned cost €1598 < €2500 budget (within budget by €902).

## Good to know
- MAAT is closed on Tuesday 2027‑05‑11 (removed from itinerary).
- Cheapest outbound flight requires an airport change (STN → LTN) during layover.
- Cheapest return flight involves three stops and two airline changes.
- Ticket prices for Lisbon Cathedral, National Museum of Archaeology and several other sights should be double‑checked on their official websites.
- No major events are listed for the travel dates.
- Before booking, check your government's official travel advice for Portugal (safety, entry rules, insurance).

## Day by day
*Days in this plan start around 09:30 and end by 22:00, at a relaxed pace. For another rhythm, tell the concierge, e.g. "we wake up early, start at 07:00", "we stay out late" or "a more relaxed pace, please".*

### Day 1 – Mon 2027‑05‑10: Baixa / Chiado
*Weather*: light rain · walking 0.3 km
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with SAS; see Getting there and back.
- **17:30 Lisbon Cathedral** – Lisbon’s oldest church, founded in 1147 after the reconquest; blends Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque elements. Open Mon–Sat 10:00‑18:30. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.patriarcado-lisboa.pt/site/index.php?id=10686)
- **20:00 Néctar WineBar** – Mid‑range wine bar, try the house‑made dessert. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)

### Day 2 – Tue 2027‑05‑11: Belém
*Weather*: drizzle · walking 12.9 km
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – UNESCO Manueline monastery built in the 16th century to celebrate Vasco da Gama’s voyage; includes the Church of Santa Maria de Belém. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). *ticket €18* [Source](http://www.patrimoniocultural.gov.pt/en/museus-e-monumentos/dgpc/m/mosteiro-dos-jeronimos/)
- **12:30 Mercado Oriental** – Street‑food market, try the Macanese stall (small dishes €3). (low budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa)
- **13:30 National Museum of Archaeology** – Largest archaeological collection in Portugal, housed in the western wing of the Jerónimos monastery; opened 1906. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.mnarqueologia-ipmuseus.pt/)
- **15:15 Navy Museum** – Maritime heritage exhibits; established 1963, includes ship models and navigation instruments. Open May‑Sep 10:00‑18:00, Oct‑Apr 10:00‑17:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://ccm.marinha.pt/pt/museu)
- **18:30 Dinner near Belém** – Snack from a nearby kiosk.

### Day 3 – Wed 2027‑05‑12: Chiado / Alfama
*Weather*: rain · walking 12.5 km
- **10:00 Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado** – Modern Portuguese and international art, covering painting, sculpture, photography and design. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/96321716)
- **12:00 Museu Arqueológico do Carmo** – Housed in a former convent ruined by the 1755 earthquake; displays archaeological finds from prehistoric to Roman times. Open Oct‑May Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:00; Jun‑Sep 10:00‑19:00. *ticket €7* [Source](https://www.museuarqueologicodocarmo.pt/)
- **13:30 Cervejaria da Trindade** – Try the codfish plate; good beer selection. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **14:30 Monumento a Camões** – Bronze statue honoring poet Luís de Camões, unveiled 1867; located in Praça Luís de Camões. [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cam%C3%B5es_Monument)
- **15:30 Monument to the Discoveries** – Iconic 1960 monument shaped like a caravel prow; climb for river views. *ticket €4* [Source](http://www.padraodosdescobrimentos.pt/)
- **16:30 Muralha Fernandina** – Medieval wall fragment built in 1373 by King Fernando I, part of Lisbon’s 14th‑century defenses. [Source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/N4845258130)
- **19:00 Belcanto** – Two‑Michelin‑star dinner; order the tasting menu. (high budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 4 – Thu 2027‑05‑13: Parque Eduardo VII
*Weather*: drizzle · walking 1.1 km
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – Interactive sport‑history exhibits. Free entry. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑17:00. [Source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966)
- **12:30 Faca & Garfo** – Grilled Portuguese specialties; good value. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **14:00 Monument aos Restauradores** – Commemorates the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. [Source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630)
- **19:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – Traditional Portuguese dishes; three‑course dinner. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)

### Day 5 – Fri 2027‑05‑14: Avenidas de Lisboa
*Weather*: overcast · walking 1.9 km
- **10:00 Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** – World‑class collections spanning antiquities, European, Islamic and modern art. Open Sun‑Mon, We‑Fr 10:00‑18:00; Sat 10:00‑21:00. *ticket price: see the website* [Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calouste_Gulbenkian_Museum)
- **12:30 Os Tibetanos** – Vegetarian/vegan friendly; try the tofu stir‑fry. (mid budget) [Source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto)
- **16:35 Depart from Lisbon** – Flight with Finnair; see Getting there and back.
